title: Kth Letter of the Shifted Echo
statement:
A string starts as "a". One round does this: take the current string, build a copy where every letter is moved one step forward in the alphabet ('a' → 'b', …, 'y' → 'z', and 'z' wraps to 'a'), and append that copy to the end.

So after one round the string is "ab", after two it is "abbc", after three "abbcbccd". The string doubles every round, forever.

Return the letter at position k, counting from 1. In this version k can be up to a billion, so building the string is not an option.

examples.why: After three rounds the string is "abbcbccd"; its 6th letter is c.
This position has been shifted 26 times, and 26 shifts take z back around to a.

hints: Write out the first 8 or 16 letters and the position of each in binary, starting from 0.
Position p (0-based) in the second half of a block of size 2^m is a shifted copy of position p − 2^m. Each time you strip the top bit, you add one shift.
The letter is 'a' shifted by the number of 1-bits in k − 1, modulo 26.

explain.intuition:
Use 0-based positions, so look at p = k − 1. After enough rounds the string has length 2^m > p. Its second half is the first half shifted by one. So if p has its top bit set, the letter at p is the letter at p with that bit cleared, plus one shift. Repeat until p is 0, which is the original 'a'.

Every 1-bit of p is cleared exactly once and adds exactly one shift. So the answer is 'a' moved forward by popcount(k − 1) steps, wrapping after 26. The wrap only shows up for huge k, which is why the third example matters.
steps: Count the 1-bits of p: repeatedly add p & 1 and shift right, or clear the lowest set bit with p & (p − 1).
Return the letter that many steps after 'a'.
pitfalls: Counting bits of k instead of k − 1. Position 1 has k = 1 (one bit) but zero shifts.
Forgetting the wrap from 'z' to 'a'. With k up to a billion a position can collect 26 or more shifts.
Building the string. It would need about a billion characters.

solutions.title: Peel off the top half
solutions.idea: Find the smallest block size 2^m that contains the position. If the position is in the second half, map it to the first half and add a shift.

solutions.title: Count the 1-bits of k − 1
solutions.idea: Each set bit of the 0-based position is one shift. Clear bits with p & (p − 1) and count.

followups: Each round now uses its own rule: some rounds append a shifted copy, others append an unchanged copy. How does the bit trick change?
Return the whole prefix of length k for small k. What is the cleanest way to build it?
lcTitle: Find the K-th Character in String Game I
